headline: Why Your New Addition's Paint Job Looks Uneven in Berkeley
articleBody:
It's frustrating when your freshly painted addition in Berkeley has an uneven finish. Oftentimes, this isn't due to poor paint quality but rather common preparation and application mistakes. Things like painting before the drywall compound is completely dry or skipping primer on new surfaces can lead to flashing or inconsistent sheen. Also, inadequate masking can cause rough edges and an unprofessional look. Even applying coatings in unsuitable temperatures or humidity can mess with the drying process, leaving you with a patchy appearance. And that 'dry to touch' feeling? It doesn't always mean the paint is fully cured, which can lead to issues down the line. Avoiding these pitfalls is key to a smooth, professional result.

What to Prepare Before You Start:
Before painting, ensure all drywall finishing is thoroughly inspected and dry – this can take at least 24 hours per coat, sometimes longer if it's cold or damp. Make sure all sanding dust is completely removed; even a little bit can ruin your finish. Protect adjacent materials like flooring or windows with proper masking. If you have new or repaired surfaces, priming is a must to get that even base. Thinking about all these steps upfront can save you a lot of headaches later on. If you're tackling a big project or have high ceilings, bringing in a pro can make a huge difference in achieving a flawless finish.
